content.text:
I reviewed the transcript, answer key, and record items, paying attention to the two figures the meeting corrected mid-conversation ($395,000 → $358,000 for the joint-account split; October 30 → October 13 for the hearing/judgment date) and to the items the client declined.

**Findings in brief:**
- All three life-event/account-action figures in the record match the *final* numbers said in the meeting ($358,000, $212,400, $45,000). Notably, record item 5 uses the corrected $358,000, not the stale $395,000.
- Six of seven action items are captured with the correct owner and the correct final due date (including the worksheet's renegotiated 9/25 date, not the originally proposed Friday 9/18).
- **Gap:** the beneficiary change (i5) — 403(b) and hospital group life from Gavin to Lucia and Mateo 50/50, to be done in the HR portal only on the day the judgment is entered — is entirely missing from the record. This is the item with the highest stakes and the trickiest timing constraint (the automatic restraining order bars an earlier change), so its omission is a material miss.
- None of the three declined/deferred items (maiden name, backup term policy on Gavin, $40,000 cash distribution) leaked into the record as actions — correctly excluded.
- One unpaired record item: life event 3, "Refinancing of home," which the transcript does establish as a settlement obligation within twelve months of the decree.

key_items.note: "Divorce settlement" captures the divorce life event. Carries no figures or dates, so nothing to be wrong; it does omit the 9/10/2026 signing and the 10/13/2026 hearing, but no incorrect figure is asserted.
Title and October 1, 2026 effective date are right. Salary step $118,000 to $127,500 is not recorded, but no wrong figure is carried.
Uses the corrected $358,000, not the superseded $395,000 the client initially recalled. In-kind, pro rata, joint to new individual account all captured.
$212,400 plus/minus gains and losses, Quillmoor to new rollover IRA, correct plan named. Matches the final decision to roll the full amount.
$45,000 of Treasury bills sold from the new individual account with proceeds to Fallowbrook savings. Figure matches the rounded-up six-month reserve.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-09-17 (tomorrow). Exhibits included in the task wording.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-09-25. Correctly uses the renegotiated date rather than the initially proposed Friday the 18th.
Owner Graciela, due 2026-10-31. Correctly reflects that Graciela took this on herself from Fallowbrook rather than Silas lining up lenders.
Owner Noor, due 2026-09-18 (Friday). All four packet components listed, including the questionnaire and IPS added later in the meeting.

Not captured anywhere in the record. Missing the beneficiary change on the 403(b) and hospital group life from Gavin to Lucia and Mateo 50/50 with her sister as custodian for Mateo, owner Graciela, timed to the day the judgment is entered (expected 10/13/2026) and not before, due to the automatic restraining order.
Owner Silas, due 2026-09-21 (Monday), comments routed to Joanna. Correct.
Owner Silas, due 2026-11-10. Wording is compressed and omits the age-65/Moderate/2033 and Social Security specifics, but it plainly captures the same deliverable for the next meeting.

extra_items.note: The transcript establishes the refinance as a settlement obligation: she keeps the house and must refinance into her sole name within twelve months of the decree, with the payment modeled moving from $2,246 to roughly $2,668. It is distinct from action item 11, which is only the loan estimate.
